A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Double Sparse Factorization (DSF) work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model pruning, image classification, matrix reconstruction, fine-tuning, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds downstream language tasks, CPU timing, memory measurements, further ablations, and LLM fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same alternating sparse-factor updates, ADMM solver, warm starts, annealing, and initialization. Input scaling and layer-wise finalization are also retained. Expanded implementation descriptions and additional fine-tuning experiments do not establish a change to the DSF compression procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds seven zero-shot tasks: BoolQ, RTE, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, and OpenBookQA (Table 2). Appendix A.7 also introduces RedPajama data for LLM fine-tuning. Existing Wikitext-2, CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and matrix-reconstruction coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SparseGPT comparisons at 50%, 40%, and 30% density, and adds Wanda at 30% density, where v1 omitted it. Existing OBC, magnitude-pruning, cyclical-pruning, and matrix-factorization comparators are retained.

E3.justification: CIFAR-10 fine-tuning remains 50 epochs, but its learning-rate schedule changes from 0.01 dropping to 0.001 after 20 epochs to 0.1 decaying linearly to zero. New protocols include zero-shot accuracy evaluation, CPU matrix-chain timing, checkpointed maximum-sequence-length tests, and LLM distillation comparing ADMM at 50% density with DSF at 45% density to approximately match storage.

E4.justification: v2 retains the finalization, fixed-mask, and iteration/annealing analyses, while adding quantitative factor-density and initialization ablations (Figures 6–7). It also adds storage-quality and pruning-time-quality analyses (Figures 3 and 8), plus CPU and fine-tuning-memory investigations in Appendices A.4–A.5.

E5.justification: Both versions report five differently seeded runs and ± values for CIFAR-10, and show means with individual observations in the retained reconstruction plots. No new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is specified. Revised ± values are result changes.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial downstream, computational-cost, ablation, and LLM fine-tuning results. For example, Table 2 reports Llama2-7B mean zero-shot accuracy of 57.78 for DSF versus 56.64 for ADMM. CIFAR-10 fine-tuned scores are revised alongside the changed schedule: at 10% density, Resnet-20-16 DSF changes from 89.3±0.3 to 89.8±0.2. These are not same-setting gains. Retained Table 1 DSF scores and ImageNet scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The constrained factorization objectives, representability arguments, ADMM updates, and Appendix A.1 Sylvester-equation derivation are retained. v2's general ADMM formulation and explicit input-rescaling equations explain existing mathematics without introducing a substantive new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal DSF contributions remain essentially unchanged. The introduction and Section 5.1 narrow the novelty claim about a pruned larger model outperforming a smaller dense model to uniform layer-wise pruning and specifically better perplexity.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's brief mask-storage discussion, v2 interprets storage-format overhead, additional activations, runtime costs, and the role of gradient checkpointing (Section 4.4 and Appendix A.5). Its conclusion newly identifies manual layer-wise sparsity allocation and unresolved integration with gradual pruning and intervening fine-tuning as limitations.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents ADMM initialization and mask-selection details, ImageNet's 20-epoch fine-tuning duration, packed-mask PyTorch storage, CPU hardware and core/frequency controls, and A100 memory-testing settings. Appendix A.7 specifies the LLM fine-tuning hardware, duration, optimizer, and token batch size. Acknowledgments add a GPU-kernel code link; the original project link remains.

R1.justification: Related work adds connections to sparse coding through Lee et al. (2006) and sparse-factorization fine-tuning through Chen et al. (2024), with additional references supporting the new experiments. Giffon et al. remains discussed in Section 2 despite losing its introductory mention. The central research positioning is retained, with a narrower uniform-pruning novelty claim.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 expands ADMM and scaling explanations, moves the matrix-approximation comparison from Section 5.3 to Appendix A.2, adjusts section titles and cross-references, and updates affiliations and conference headers. These are targeted revisions rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds storage-quality, factor-density, initialization, and pruning-time plots, together with zero-shot, CPU-runtime, memory, and LLM fine-tuning tables. Table 1 gains comparator rows. Existing figures are resized or redrawn, and the matrix-comparison plot moves to the appendix with a shorter vertical range. The ambiguous ImageNet row label 'FT' is corrected to 'Magnitude w/o FT'.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for DSF's practical value. v1 mainly established accuracy advantages at matched nonzero counts; v2 adds storage-matched comparisons, measured CPU costs and memory limits, downstream language tasks, and LLM fine-tuning validation. Additional ablations and explicit limitations make design choices and deployment tradeoffs more assessable. CPU-chain benchmarks still leave end-to-end LLM speed uncertain, but the added evidence addresses a central weakness of the efficiency argument.
